variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: First update remaining_path according to the policy prompt for memory. If its first letter is A, select A: move to the nearest robot-left target clockwise. If B, select B: move to the nearest robot-right target clockwise. If C, select C: move to the nearest robot-left target counterclockwise. If D, select D: move to the nearest robot-right target counterclockwise. These conditions apply regardless of the preceding subgoal: after any completed A, B, C, or D, transition to whichever letter now leads remaining_path. The current highlighted target is the departure site, not the destination. Robot-left selects the adjacent target with larger x and robot-right the adjacent target with smaller x; the menu handles these targets internally and requires no point. Initial subgoals decoded from the demonstrations are B for episode 0, A for episode 19, D for episode 58, A for episode 86, and A for episode 99. Never infer the next direction solely from the current location: identical locations can require different moves on repeated visits. If the list is empty, the demonstrated route is complete and no further traversal is intended. If an unexpected situation nevertheless requires a menu answer, or the demonstration cannot be decoded, choose A if a larger-x adjacent target exists, otherwise B if a smaller-x adjacent target exists, otherwise A; this is only a deterministic fallback, not an additional demonstrated move.

fields.name: remaining_path
fields.description: When memory is empty and demonstration frames are present, decode the entire demonstration in two stages. First construct a temporary traversal ledger from the demonstration alone, excluding the reset to the execution starting scene. Anchor the ledger at the initial demonstrated highlighted target and initial wrist position, before any arrival change. Identify that starting target and every chronological arrival through the final demonstration arrival, identifying sites by stable horizontal order rather than exact fluctuating coordinates. The first distinct arrival closes the first traversal from this initial scene; it does not begin the route. Each consecutive pair of distinct adjacent sites creates one ledger row, even if that pair or destination has appeared before. Complete this arrival ledger before classifying any traversal; never compress its repeated rows. The ledger is temporary reasoning at this decision, not an additional memory field. Use highlight changes together with wrist arrival and subsequent motion to resolve each reached site. Temporary double highlights must not erase an arrival boundary. Suppress only coordinate jitter and duplicate indications of the same arrival; preserve every return to a previously visited site, immediate reversal, and repeated crossing as a separate traversal. Do not combine traversals into a net excursion. Second classify each ledger row independently. For that crossing, identify its departure and destination target sites, representative resting wrist positions at those endpoints, and intermediate wrist samples belonging to that crossing. Write any positions as [y, x]. Compute destination target x minus departure target x to determine horizontal direction; do not use a local reversal in wrist x. Judge the arc using the substantial interior wrist excursion relative to the line joining that row's endpoint wrist positions, not a near-arrival sample that may belong to the next crossing. For endpoint wrist positions [y0, x0] and [y1, x1] and an interior wrist sample [ys, xs], when x1 differs from x0, baseline_y = y0 + (y1 - y0) * (xs - x0) / (x1 - x0). Negative ys minus baseline_y indicates upper; positive indicates lower. Use wrist coordinates throughout this baseline calculation. Reversing horizontal direction does not by itself change the side of the baseline occupied by the arc. Use this table: larger x plus upper arc = A; larger x plus lower arc = C; smaller x plus upper arc = D; smaller x plus lower arc = B. Larger x is robot-left and smaller x is robot-right. Do not infer an arc from the preceding traversal, the net excursion, or a waypoint. Do not confuse the wrist with the attached stick endpoint or compare wrist height directly with target coordinates to classify the arc. Write exactly one letter per ledger row in chronological order. Verify a one-to-one correspondence between rows and letters, retaining every repeated crossing and the row ending at the final demonstration arrival. Explicitly check that the first row covers the motion from the demonstration's initial scene to its first distinct arrival, and that its independently classified letter is the first entry of the list. Keep this entry even though it is also the command being selected now. Before committing the list, verify every letter against its own demonstration segment, not just the first letter. First check the departure and destination target x values: smaller destination x permits only B or D; larger destination x permits only A or C. Independently check the intermediate wrist trajectory against the baseline joining that segment's endpoint wrist resting positions: upper selects D for smaller x or A for larger x; lower selects B for smaller x or C for larger x. Correct any letter that fails either check. Recheck both properties for every segment, including successive moves in the same horizontal direction and moves immediately after reversals; neither direction nor arc may be copied from a neighboring traversal. Write the full list at this first decision, without deleting the move selected now. On a later decision with carried memory, the intervening execution shows the preceding oracle command completed at its adjacent target; remove exactly one leading letter from the carried list before selecting the next command. The decision-step protocol guarantees that each such return follows one completed command, so do not count individual frames or repeated highlights as additional completions. If there is no intervening completed execution, retain the carried list. Once exhausted, write []. Use a canonical textual format for the list: square brackets, single-quoted uppercase letters, and a comma followed by one space between entries. This formatting does not change which traversals the list contains or when entries are removed. e.g. ['A', 'B', 'A', 'D']
fields.annotation: An ordered list of menu letters encoding the demonstrated traversals not yet completed in execution, including the traversal to command at this decision step. Decode the demonstration into individual moves between adjacent target sites, preserving repeated visits and reversals. Larger destination x means robot-left; smaller destination x means robot-right. A leftward move along the image-upper arc is A, a rightward move along the image-lower arc is B, a leftward move along the image-lower arc is C, and a rightward move along the image-upper arc is D. Judge the arc from the intermediate wrist trajectory relative to the line joining its resting positions at the two target sites, not by comparing wrist height directly with target coordinates. Target highlight changes identify arrivals; small coordinate fluctuations and briefly simultaneous highlights do not constitute extra moves. At the first execution decision, record the entire decoded demonstration. At each subsequent decision, remove the single leading move completed during the intervening oracle execution. Do not remove the move being chosen at the current decision. Use a canonical textual format for the list: square brackets, single-quoted uppercase letters, and a comma followed by one space between entries. Thus episode 0 has ['B', 'B'] then ['B']; episode 19 has ['A', 'B', 'A', 'D'], ['B', 'A', 'D'], ['A', 'D'], ['D']; episode 58 has ['D', 'D', 'A', 'A'], ['D', 'A', 'A'], ['A', 'A'], ['A']; episode 86 has ['A', 'C', 'A', 'B', 'D'], ['C', 'A', 'B', 'D'], ['A', 'B', 'D'], ['B', 'D'], ['D']; episode 99 has ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D'], ['B', 'C', 'D'], ['C', 'D'], ['D']. After the final traversal completes, the value is []. e.g. ['A', 'B', 'A', 'D']

history.critique:
field remaining_path, POLICY PROMPT
  The failures occurred at initialization while reproducing a demonstrated stick-navigation route. Two successive larger-x lower-arc moves were decoded as B,B instead of C,C; an initial smaller-x upper-arc move was decoded as B instead of D; seven traversals containing repeated returns were compressed into three; and a final smaller-x upper-arc move was recorded as B instead of D. The annotations retained the complete correctly decoded routes. These errors break PREDICTABILITY of the initial memory and, when the first letter is wrong, SUFFICIENCY for selecting the first subgoal. Strengthen initialization with an explicit two-stage decoding procedure. First identify the chronological sequence of target arrivals across the entire demonstration, keeping each visit, immediate reversal, and repeated crossing as a separate traversal. A temporary double highlight must not erase an arrival boundary: use wrist arrival and subsequent motion to resolve which adjacent site was reached. Suppress only coordinate jitter and duplicate indications of the same arrival, not returns to previously visited sites. Then classify EACH traversal independently using destination minus departure target x and the intermediate wrist arc relative to the line between resting wrist positions. Use this explicit table: larger x plus upper arc = A; larger x plus lower arc = C; smaller x plus upper arc = D; smaller x plus lower arc = B. Upper means smaller image y than that baseline, not smaller y than a target. Do not infer the arc from the preceding traversal, the net excursion, or a waypoint. Verify that the number of letters equals the number of adjacent-site traversals, including the final arrival. For example, alternating upper-arc smaller-x and larger-x crossings, followed by a lower-arc larger-x return, another upper-arc smaller-x crossing, and two upper-arc larger-x moves yields ["D","A","D","C","D","A","A"]. The field continues to hold the ordered demonstrated traversals not yet completed, including the one selected now. Initialize the entire list when demonstration frames and empty incoming memory are present. At each later decision following one completed oracle execution, remove exactly one leading letter; do not remove the newly selected letter. Retain the list if no command completed, and write [] after the final completion. No additional memory fields are needed.

history.critique:
field remaining_path, POLICY PROMPT
  At the first decision, the goal required reproducing the demonstrated path around the sticks. The policy selected the correct first command but sometimes wrote an incorrect later suffix: it assigned a larger-x letter to a smaller-x crossing, reused an upper-arc letter for a later lower arc, or swapped the upper/lower letters on successive larger-x crossings. The annotated routes preserved those direction and arc changes. These are failures of reliably predicting the memory, not evidence that another memory field is needed. Strengthen the initial decoding procedure with an independent per-traversal verification before writing the list. For each pair of consecutive reached sites, determine the sign of destination target x minus departure target x first: smaller x restricts the letter to B or D, and larger x restricts it to A or C. Then independently determine the arc from intermediate wrist positions relative to the line between the endpoint wrist positions: smaller image y selects the upper arc, larger image y the lower arc. Apply the table explicitly: smaller x/upper = D; smaller x/lower = B; larger x/upper = A; larger x/lower = C. Verify every letter against both tests, including later crossings with unchanged horizontal direction and crossings immediately after reversals; neither arc nor direction may be copied from a neighboring traversal. Initialize it with the entire verified route, for example ["B","C","A"] for a smaller-x lower crossing followed by larger-x lower and larger-x upper crossings. At each later decision following one completed oracle execution, remove exactly one leading letter; retain the list if no execution completed, and write [] when exhausted. Do not delete the currently selected command.

refused
  No annotation-rule or subgoal-policy prompt change is warranted. The recorded routes agree with the demonstrated arrivals, horizontal directions, and wrist arcs, and the first subgoal was correct in every reported case. The existing memory already contains the ordered information needed later; the errors were in applying the decoding table, so additional fields and episode-specific route exceptions are not justified. One flagged initial decision returned both the correct first command D and the correct memory ["D","D","D"], and reported no missing information.
